lead.t: Aspergillosis is recognized in tissue by the presence of:

b: Agent: Aspergillus fumigatus (most common), A. flavus , A. niger , A. terreus
Deuteromycetes; septate hyphae with characteristic conidiophores
Ubiquitous in environment — soil, decaying organic matter, air
Diagnosis: Culture, microscopy (septate hyphae with 45° branching), galactomannan antigen detection in blood/BAL, CT scan (halo sign in invasive form)
Treatment: Voriconazole (drug of choice for invasive); itraconazole (ABPA, aspergilloma); Amphotericin B (alternative)

year-old leukemia patient post bone marrow transplant on cyclosporine and prednisone with pneumonia, KOH shows septate hyphae with parallel walls and low-angle branching: Aspergillus fumigatus

snip.t: Aspergillosis is recognized in tissue by the presence of:
Fungal spores are significant allergens — can cause allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), farmer's lung, bronchial asthma
Allergic: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) (central bronchiectasis in asthma)

| Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) | Asthma, fleeting pulmonary infiltrates, eosinophilia, high total IgE, Aspergillus‑specific IgE | Central bronchiectasis on CT plus immunologic markers; response to steroids distinguishes it. |
Antigen detection: Rapid and sensitive for some infections (e.g., Cryptococcal antigen in CSF/serum, Galactomannan for invasive aspergillosis, Histoplasma antigen in urine/serum).
Specific agents: For infections like aspergillosis (e.g., voriconazole) or mucormycosis (e.g., posaconazole, amphotericin B).
–Detecting the pulmonary infiltrates associated with allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis.
•Oral itraconazole should be contemplated in patients with allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA).

qs.q: A 58-year-old stem cell transplant recipient with invasive pulmonary aspergillosis experiences persistent disease despite voriconazole therapy. Which intravenous antifungal drug is most appropriate to add or substitute?
qs.e: Caspofungin is an echinocandin that inhibits beta-1,3-glucan synthase and is indicated for azole-refractory invasive aspergillosis. Fluconazole lacks reliable activity against Aspergillus species entirely.

qs.q: Which fungal species is recognized as the most common etiological agent responsible for invasive aspergillosis in immunocompromised hosts?
qs.e: Aspergillus fumigatus is the most common cause of invasive aspergillosis. Madurella mycetomatis is primarily associated with eumycetoma rather than primary invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Fundamentals: Fungi, Antifungal Drugs & More: MCQs

qs.q: A 45-year-old immunocompromised patient is diagnosed with invasive aspergillosis. Which antifungal agent is considered the first-line treatment choice?
qs.e: Voriconazole is the established first-line treatment for aspergillosis infections. Fluconazole lacks adequate activity against Aspergillus species.

qs.q: Aspergillosis is recognized in tissue by the presence of:
qs.e: Aspergillus species are characterized by septate hyphae with dichotomous (acute-angled) branching. Broad, sparsely septate hyphae are seen in Zygomycetes; yeast cells with single budding are typical of Candida; and spherules with endospores are seen in Coccidioides.

qs.q: Invasive aspergillosis in a neutropenic patient is angioinvasive. The characteristic CT finding in early disease is
o: Halo sign — ground-glass opacity surrounding a nodule
Eggshell calcification of hilar lymph nodes
qs.e: The "halo sign" on CT (ground-glass opacity surrounding a pulmonary nodule) is characteristic of early invasive aspergillosis. The "air-crescent sign" appears later. Aspergillus shows septate hyphae branching at 45 degrees.

qs.q: Which antifungal is first-line treatment for invasive aspergillosis?
qs.e: Voriconazole is the first-line treatment for invasive aspergillosis. Diagnosis is supported by galactomannan antigen and beta-D-glucan in serum or BAL. Aspergillus shows septate hyphae branching at 45-degree angles.

qs.q: Aspergillosis is recognized in tissue by the presence of: Aspergillus shows septate hyphae with acute-angle (45°) branching in tissue. ---
qs.e: Aspergillus is identified in tissue by septate hyphae with acute-angle branching.

qs.q: Which statement regarding aspergillosis is correct? Aspergillus causes a wide range of local infections (otomycosis, keratitis, onychomycosis, sinusitis) beyond invasive pulmonary disease; blood cultures are usually negative even in invasive disease, so c is false. ---
o: Clinical manifestations include local infections of the ear and sinuses
Bone marrow transplant recipients are not at risk for invasive disease
Patients on parenteral corticosteroids are not at risk for invasive disease
Pulmonary aspergillosis is frequently diagnosed by culturing blood samples
Patients with allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis rarely have eosinophilia
qs.e: Aspergillus species frequently cause localized infections involving the ear, cornea, nails, and sinuses in addition to pulmonary manifestations.
